title: Notable dates replace the recently written list

history.detail:
CONDITIONAL: QA1 gate-1 audit, Sprint 45, commit a8f063f (main HEAD, clean tree). Verdict: CONDITIONAL. Two small required fixes; everything else passes.

Sprint file: re-read fresh. It is unchanged since Dev Team 1's start (0d70053) apart from the lifecycle status line.

Handoff: read at a8f063f with git show. It has a Round 1 section quoting VERIFY PASS (lint, typecheck, test, build) exit=0 with 43 files and 502 tests. QA1's own npm run verify at a8f063f: verify=0, 43 files, 502 tests, VERIFY PASS.

REQUIRED FIX 1, R8's acceptance grep is not met, and the handoff misreports its result.
The handoff's R8 row says: grep -rn "get_recent_reading_dates\|RecentReadingDate\|Recently written" app lib gives exit 1. QA1 ran exactly that command at a8f063f. It gives exit 0, with one match:
  app/date/[date]/notable-dates-page.test.ts:60: expect(fake.rpc).not.toHaveBeenCalledWith("get_recent_reading_dates");
So the acceptance criterion ("grep finds no get_recent_reading_dates ... in app/ or lib/") is not met as written, and the handoff states a check result that the command doesn't produce. Under this project's evidence standard (CLAUDE.md, after Sprint 34), a reported exit code has to be the real one.
The intent of R8 is clearly met: the app never calls the RPC, and that line is a negative assertion proving it. The cleanest fix also makes the test stronger. Replace the negative assertion with an allow-list: assert that every RPC the fake received is one of get_reading_by_date and get_adjacent_reading_dates. That removes the string, and it catches any future unexpected RPC, not just this one.
Do not obfuscate the string just to satisfy grep.

REQUIRED FIX 2, the handoff.
Add a Round 2 section, leaving Round 1 untouched. It should report the real grep result after fix 1 (exit 1), plus verify's final line with exit=0.

Everything else, met:

R1/R9: met. QA1 parsed R1's table from the sprint file and the NOTABLE_DATES entries from lib/date-page/notable-dates.ts. There are 20 and 20, and the two are identical in order, dates and text, including the straight quotes around "I Have a Dream". notable-dates.test.ts covers the count, parseDatePageParam, strictly ascending order with no duplicates, and the exact text.

R2: met. notable-dates.ts has no import statements (grep of ^import finds none; the "from" hits are prose). DateNavigation no longer returns null on "unavailable": it renders the strip with only Previous/Next omitted. notable-dates-page.test.ts runs the real DatePage with the adjacent lookup paused, and both copies keep all 20 links. The outage evidence (outage-report.json) agrees.

R3: met. The desktop copy is in the strip under the picker, with the heading "Other notable dates" and the same list and link styles (the old recent* rules were renamed, values unchanged). Each link has aria-describedby pointing at a role=tooltip span holding the description. The CSS shows it on .notableItem:hover and .notableLink:focus-visible + .notableTooltip, hiding it with visibility, so the description is still computed while hidden. There is no title attribute. The handoff's CDP probe reports Chrome's accessibility tree giving description "D-Day: the Allies land in Normandy" for the focused link. QA1 viewed desktop-1280-tooltip-keyboard.png: the tooltip is open under 6 June 1944 on keyboard focus.

R4: met. NotableDatesSection is passed as ReadingView's new afterBody, rendered as main's last child after the .body div that holds the reading section, and therefore outside the reading section and its sticky reveal. It is mobileOnly, with no details element. The heading uses readingStyles.sectionTitle, and each row shows the description as a visible second line inside the link, at least 44px. The page test pins the markup order (the reading section closes, then the notable nav). QA1 viewed phone-390-notable-section.png: 20 rows, descriptions visible, 20 July 1969 marked. With no Previous/Next, the strip wrapper is desktopOnly, so phones get no empty strip.

R5: met. On 1969-07-20 both copies render a span with aria-current="page", not a link, and keep the description (tooltip on desktop, visible line on phones). There are tests for both.
- Answer to Dev Team's question 1: a hover-only tooltip on the unlinked current date is acceptable. R5 asks that its description still shows, and it does on hover, while the page itself is about that date. Don't add a tabindex 0 to a non-link span: a focus stop that does nothing is worse for keyboard users than the gap it closes.

R6: met. Both copies use datePagePath(date) with prefetch={false}.

R7: met. The Previous/Next markup, labels, rel and placement are unchanged; the wrapper became a nav with its own label. navigation.test.ts's Previous/Next assertions are unchanged. The calls dropped the recent argument, and isoDate too, because shapeDateNavigation no longer takes it. That's a necessary consequence of R8's removal, not a behaviour change.

R8 (apart from fix 1): RecentReadingDate, recent, the sort and the RPC call are removed. loadDateNavigation makes one RPC. The nav labels are now "Previous and next readings" and aria-labelledby on the notable heading. supabase/migrations is unchanged between 0d70053 and a8f063f (git diff --quiet exit 0).

R10: met. The README never described the old list or its RPC (the handoff's grep; QA1 agrees no README change was needed).

R11: both required screenshots are committed and QA1 opened them.

Non-blocking notes:
- WCAG 1.4.13: the tooltip can't be dismissed with Escape without client JS. This is disclosed, and R3 doesn't require it.
- Watch item for LiveQA: the tooltips are absolutely positioned and only visibility-hidden, so they still count toward the page's scrollable width. At 1280px the probe shows docW 1280, equal to vw, so there's no overflow there. At narrower desktop widths (901 to 1279px), a tooltip belonging to the last item on a wrapped row could reach past the card's right edge. LiveQA should check for horizontal scroll at roughly 1000px. This is not demonstrated as a defect, so it isn't part of this verdict.
- The formatLongDateText move to format.ts is a reasonable shared helper, with its own test.

No Human Prerequisites.

PASS: QA1 gate-1 re-audit, Sprint 45, round 2, commit 947f5ea (main HEAD, clean tree). Verdict: PASS.

Sprint file: re-read fresh. It is unchanged since Dev Team 1's start (0d70053); git diff 0d70053 947f5ea -- docs/sprints shows only state/sprint-45.json.

What moved since round 1 (a8f063f): only the two fixes QA1 required.
- app/date/[date]/notable-dates-page.test.ts: the negative assertion on the retired RPC is replaced with an allow-list. It collects every RPC name the fake received and asserts the set equals {get_reading_by_date, get_adjacent_reading_dates}. Any other call fails, and the string is gone rather than disguised.
- docs/handoffs/sprint-45.md: a new Round 2 section, appended (18 insertions, 0 deletions, so Round 1 is untouched). It quotes VERIFY PASS ... exit=0 with 43 files and 502 tests, and states round 1's error plainly: the grep was run before the test file added a match, and the earlier result was reported without re-running.
- Plus the state file. Nothing else changed.

Fix 1, verified: QA1 ran grep -rn "get_recent_reading_dates\|RecentReadingDate\|Recently written" app lib at 947f5ea, unpiped: no output, grep exit=1. R8's acceptance criterion is now met as written. Behaviour is still covered, more strongly than before.

Fix 2, verified: Round 2 was read from the commit with git show, and its grep claim matches QA1's own run.

Checks: QA1's own npm run verify at 947f5ea gave verify=0, 43 files, 502 tests, VERIFY PASS.

All other requirements stand as recorded in round 1's notes (R1-R7, R9-R11 met; QA1's ruling on Dev Team's question 1 unchanged). The non-blocking notes carry over:
- Escape dismissal (WCAG 1.4.13) isn't possible without client JS.
- LiveQA watch item: check for horizontal scroll at roughly 1000px desktop width. As Dev Team's Round 2 note says, the desktop .card is a fixed 1320px (pre-existing), so attribute any scroll at 901-1319px to the card or to the tooltips before calling it.

CONDITIONAL: CONDITIONAL (round 1). One defect. LiveQA steps 1 to 4 all pass on production.
The defect: on desktop widths from 901 to about 1278px, the hidden tooltips make the whole page scroll sideways. This is QA1's watch item, confirmed live and attributed below. It is new in this sprint.

Tested 2026-11-24, about 16:15 to 16:35 UTC, against https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app.
Shipped commit 947f5ea. Production serves the pushed tip ec3ddec: /api/health/db reports status ok, connected true, commit ec3ddec, with migrationVersion unchanged at 20261122152710_navigation_exact_date_readings. git diff --stat 947f5ea origin/main touches only docs/sprints/state/sprint-45.json.
Tools: headless Chromium (Playwright 1.57) at 901, 1000, 1100, 1200, 1279, 1280, 1320 and 1440 wide; at 390x844 (isMobile, hasTouch) with JS on and off; and CDP Accessibility.getFullAXTree.

DEFECT: horizontal page scroll at 901-1278px, caused by the visibility-hidden tooltips.
What I saw, on /date/1969-07-20 (document scrollWidth against viewport width):
- 901: 969, and a visitor can scroll 68px sideways (window.scrollTo(500,0) gave scrollX 68).
- 1000: 1001, scrollable by 1px.
- 1100: 1114, scrollable by 14px.
- 1200: 1242, scrollable by 42px.
- 1279, 1280, 1320 and 1440: equal to the viewport, so no scroll.
/date/2026-12-16 and /date/1912-04-15 give the same figures (901 is 913 on 2026-12-16).
Attribution:
- In every case, scrollWidth equals exactly the right edge of the furthest tooltip, measured with getBoundingClientRect.
- Setting every [role=tooltip] to display none brings scrollWidth back to the viewport width at all those widths.
- It is not the card: at 901 the card is 821 wide and ends at x=861. Dev Team's Round 2 note says the card is a fixed 1320px; measured live, it isn't, at these widths.
- The tooltips past the viewport belong to the last link on a wrapped row:
  - at 901: "D-Day: the Allies land in Normandy" (right 943), "Yuri Gagarin becomes the first person in space" (939) and "Nelson Mandela is released from prison" (969);
  - at 1100: the Kennedy one (1114);
  - at 1200: the Challenger one (1242).
What a visitor sees: scrolled sideways at 901, the whole page shifts 68px left. The card's left edge, including the banner portrait, is cut off, and an empty band shows on the right. Screenshots: s45-901-scrolled-right.png and s45-1200-scrolled-right.png.
Also: when the overflowing tooltip is actually shown, hovering 11 February 1990 at 1000 puts it at x 730-1001 in a 1000 viewport, cut off by 1px (s45-1000-hover-overflow.png). At 901 the overflow is wider (969), so the same tooltip is cut off by up to 68px.
Repro: open /date/1969-07-20 in a desktop browser about 900-1250px wide (above the 900px phone breakpoint), then scroll right with a trackpad or shift+wheel.
What would fix it, not prescribed: keep tooltips inside the card or viewport (for example, anchor the tooltips near the right edge to the right). Or take hidden tooltips out of layout overflow, for example by clipping the strip with overflow-x clip, while keeping them in the accessibility tree; aria-describedby works even on display:none targets.

STEP 1, desktop 1280 on /date/1969-07-20: PASS.
- "Other notable dates" is an H2 in a visible desktopOnly nav, labelled by that heading. It lists 20 entries, oldest first, from 15 April 1912 to 11 March 2020.
- Each link's href is /date/<iso>, and each description (read through aria-describedby) matches R1's text exactly, including the straight quotes in "I Have a Dream".
- 20 July 1969 is a span with aria-current="page", not a link, and keeps its description ("Apollo 11 lands on the Moon").
- "Recently written" doesn't appear anywhere in the page HTML.
- The navs are labelled "Previous and next readings" and "Other notable dates".
- Hover: on 6 June 1944 the tooltip changes from visibility hidden to visible, reading "D-Day: the Allies land in Normandy", and goes back to hidden when the mouse moves off. Screenshot: s45-hover-1280.png.
- Keyboard: from a blurred page, the 9th Tab press focused 15 April 1912, and its tooltip "The Titanic sinks in the North Atlantic" became visible. The next Tab moved to 28 June 1914, showing its tooltip and hiding the previous one. Screenshot: s45-focus-1280.png.
- Screen reader, via the accessibility tree: link name "15 April 1912", description "The Titanic sinks in the North Atlantic". The same holds for 1914 and 1944.

STEP 2, three links from the 1969-07-20 list: PASS. None was refused, and each already has a saved horoscope ("Revealed on request" is present), so no write was needed:
- 1912-04-15: "this exact date", with 1912's event "More than 1,500 people on the Titanic died when the passenge...".
- 1961-04-12: "this exact date", with 1961's event "Aboard Vostok 1, Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin performed the...".
- 2020-03-11: "this exact date", with two 2020 WHO events.
On each landed page, its own date is the aria-current entry in the list.

STEP 3, phone 390, with JS and without: PASS.
- The desktopOnly notable nav isn't visible. Previous/Next are visible: "← PREVIOUS READING 24 November 1963" and "NEXT READING → 1 September 1969".
- After the reading section, outside it and not inside a details element, a visible nav has the H2 "Other notable dates" (21px, Cormorant Garamond) and 20 rows. Each row shows its description as a second visible line, for example "15 April 1912 / The Titanic sinks in the North Atlantic". Every row is 63px tall. 20 July 1969 is marked as current.
- scrollWidth is 390, so there is no sideways scroll on phones.
- Screenshots: s45-phone-notable.png and s45-phone-top.png.

STEP 4, Previous and Next: PASS.
- On /date/1969-07-20, prev is /date/1963-11-24 and next is /date/1969-09-01.
- Clicking prev lands on a saved reading whose own next is /date/1969-07-20.
- Clicking next lands on a saved reading whose own prev is /date/1969-07-20.
- So they are the neighbouring written readings.

R2's unavailable case (navigation lookups failing) can't be triggered on production; QA1's page test and outage evidence carry it.

No console or page errors on any page tested.

PASS: PASS, live-loop audit of 8920e16 (fix for LiveQA round 1 CONDITIONAL). Not a fresh gate-1 pass and not a substitute for LiveQA's retest.

Sprint file: re-read fresh. Unchanged since my gate-1 PASS (last touched 0d70053, the start commit). No new or amended requirements.

Handoff: read at the audited commit (git show 8920e16:docs/handoffs/sprint-45.md). A Round 3 section was added. Rounds 1 and 2 are untouched (54 insertions, 0 deletions). It quotes VERIFY PASS (lint, typecheck, test, build) exit=0. It also corrects Round 2's wrong claim that the card is a fixed 1320px, which LiveQA disproved live.

Diff 947f5ea..8920e16, outside excluded bookkeeping and evidence files: app/date/[date]/date.module.css (+38/-7) and a comment in NotableDates.tsx. No markup, logic or test changes. The other files in the range are sprint 46's own planning and state files, and sprint 45's state file.

The fix, checked against the defect LiveQA recorded:
1. Closed tooltips are now display:none, not visibility:hidden. A box with display:none generates no layout, so it can't contribute to scrollWidth. That removes the exact cause LiveQA attributed: scrollWidth equalled the right edge of the furthest hidden tooltip. Hover and focus selectors are unchanged and now set display:block.
   Accessibility: accname step 2A includes a hidden node when aria-describedby references it, so link descriptions survive. The handoff's AX-tree check shows 19 links with descriptions (the 20th date is the current-page span), which is consistent with that.
2. Inside @supports (position-area: block-end) and (anchor-scope: all), each li is a scoped anchor. The tooltip uses position-area block-end span-inline-end, with position-try-fallbacks flip-inline. main:has(.notableStrip) becomes position:relative, so the card is the containing block.
   I checked the claim that this moves nothing else. A grep of app CSS for absolute, fixed and sticky finds only these other absolute elements:
   - reading.module.css balanceFill: it has its own position:relative parent (balanceTrack), so it's unaffected.
   - chartTabs visuallyHidden: it has no insets, so it sits at its static position and is unaffected.
   Sticky elements don't depend on the containing block. Making main relative without a z-index creates no stacking context. The claim holds.
3. Browsers without anchor positioning fall back to the old placement. With fix 1, closed tooltips still can't widen the page there. An OPEN tooltip on the last date of a wrapped row can still run past the card while it's hovered. The handoff names this honestly as a known limitation.

Tests: no new unit test, which is justified. The change is CSS only, and Vitest renders markup without layout. The evidence is Dev Team's committed CDP probe (cdp45-overflow.mjs) and round3-overflow-report.json, which I read:
- At 901, 1000, 1100, 1200, 1279, 1280, 1320 and 1440px, with every tooltip closed, docW equals vw at every width. At 901 it's 901, where LiveQA measured 969.
- Across all 20 hovers at every width: exactly one tooltip is shown, it sits flush under its date, and it lies inside the card and the viewport. maxDocWWhileOpen equals vw.
- At 901, the flipped dates are exactly the three LiveQA saw overflow.
The phone report is said to be identical to round 1's. I didn't re-run the browser probe myself; that's static-audit scope, and LiveQA's retest covers it.

My own check: npm run verify at 8920e16, on a clean tree. Result: verify=0, VERIFY PASS (lint, typecheck, test, build) exit=0, 43 test files and 502 tests passed.

For LiveQA's retest:
(a) Re-measure scrollWidth at 901-1278 on production, closed and while hovering the rightmost date on each row.
(b) Check that every link still has its description in the AX tree, now that closed tooltips are display:none.
(c) Firefox, if you can: whether anchor positioning applies there, or the fallback runs. If it's the fallback, expect the known limitation: an open tooltip can run past the card's edge while hovered, though closed tooltips can't widen the page.
